newsitem.title: GREECE: Several Greek brokers barred from trade Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Several Greek brokers barred from trade Tuesday.

text.p: Several member firms of the Athens stock exchange were barred from trading on Tuesday after failing to comply with clearing deadlines and regulations, brokers said.
Among them was N.Devletoglou, one of the bourse's largest firms.

"We were not allowed to trade on Tuesday because we failed to deliver shares to the clearing house in 48 hours after the sale," Alexander Devletoglou, managing director of N. Devletoglou told Reuters.
"We had sales from our foreign clients and got the shares from their custodians yesterday at 15:00 local but the bourse had closed at 14:30, so we delivered today," he said.
ure to deliver by the 14:30 local closing time for the state-run bourse prompted authorities to exclude Devletoglou from trading on Tuesday.
"Our foreign clients are finding it extremely difficult to manage with the very tight 48-hour settlement deadline," said Devletoglou.
Pegasos Securities and others were also stopped from trading for the day because of similar problems meeting clearing house regulations.
Implementation of settlement regulations has been tightened since the Delta Securities scandal early this month.
Delta attempted to make settlement payment with 2.6 billion drachmas in bad cheques and three of its top officials have been charged with fraud.

Authorities have ordered audits of brokerages to track down who was on the other side of the Delta trades and to investigate allegations of widespread illegal short-selling in the market. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
